findings.title: Exhausted recovery codes are deleted only from local storage
findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` now returns a user-storage credential before a local one, but when all codes are used this branch still calls `credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...)`. That method removes only locally stored credentials, so for a federated credential the delete is a no-op: the exhausted credential remains in user storage. A later login can then reach `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`, where `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()` has no value and throws. The user-storage path needs a federated-aware removal/disable operation instead of local deletion.

findings.title: User storage receives raw recovery codes instead of hashed credential data
findings.body: The user-storage branch serializes `generatedCodes`, i.e. the plaintext recovery codes, into the `UserCredentialModel`. The local branch instead persists `credentialModel`, whose codes were hashed by `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues`. The new test provider follows the user-storage path by storing this raw JSON directly as `credentialData` and validating by plaintext comparison, so this PR establishes a path where usable recovery codes are stored unhashed in user storage and the hashed model/used-flag metadata is lost. The helper should pass the hashed credential data, or the hashing contract must be explicit and the test storage must not persist plaintext codes.

findings.title: Federated recovery-code test does not verify one-time use
findings.body: The new `isValid` implementation returns true whenever the submitted code matches any stored raw code, but never marks that code as used or updates `MyUser.recoveryCodes`; `getCredentials` also rebuilds every code as unused via `createFromValues`. The added integration test performs only one successful login, so it would pass even though the same recovery code remains reusable and the all-codes-used reconfiguration path is never exercised. The user-storage test provider should persist used state, or the test should assert that a previously used code is rejected, so the federated path actually covers the one-time-use guarantee.
